title: Maryland PSC Order No. 92514 (Case No. 9870)
text:

BEFORE THE 
PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION 
OF MARYLAND 
_______ 
Case No. 9870 
_______ 

Issue Date: July 9, 2026 
ORDER ON PROCEDURAL SCHEDULE 
On July 7, 2026, the Commission held a pre-hearing conference in the above-
captioned proceeding to establish a procedural schedule, consider any petitions to 
intervene, and address any other pending preliminary matters. Counsel for The Potomac 
Edison Company (“Potomac Edison”), the Department of Natural Resources Power Plant 
Research Program (“PPRP”), the Maryland Office of People’s Counsel (“OPC”), and the 
Commission’s Technical Staff (“Staff”) appeared on behalf of their respective parties. 
After discussing the merits of a proposed procedural schedule, Staff read the 
schedule into the record. Staff further stated that, if the parties are unable to reach a 
settlement by November 16, 2027 a status and settlement conference would be held 
instead, at which time the Commission would establish the remainder of the procedural 
schedule. 
The Commission hereby approves the partial procedural schedule articulated 
below. Discovery by Potomac Edison, PPRP, OPC, and Staff has already commenced. 
The discovery procedure is as follows: 
(1) 
responses to data requests served before September 30, 2027, 
(Direct Testimony of Staff, OPC, PPRP and any intervenors) shall 
be due within five (5) business days; 

2 

(2) 
responses to data requests served on and after September 30, 2027, 
shall be due within five (5) business days, with objections due 
within three (3) business days; 

(3) 
responses to discovery requests shall be provided electronically to 
all parties, all spreadsheets with formulae intact, unless a hard copy 
of the responses is requested to be served; and 

(4) 
the parties are directed to consult with each other and attempt in 
good faith to resolve all disputes prior to making an objection and 
again prior to filing a motion seeking relief. 

All testimony and discovery shall be served electronically on each of the parties 
to avoid delay in receipt, unless the parties agree to a different format. Parties shall 
ensure that the correct email of the person(s) to whom the testimony and discovery 
should be sent are updated and current on the service list for this matter. 
IT IS, THEREFORE, this 9th day of July in the year Two Thousand Twenty-Six, 
by the Public Service Commission of Maryland, ORDERED: 
(1) 
that parties shall file pleadings in this proceeding as follows: 

(a) 
Potomac Edison shall file Supplemental Direct Testimony 
by August 31, 2026;0F1 

(b) 
PPRP shall file updated Completeness Determination by 
September 28, 2026; and 

(c) 
Staff, OPC, PPRP, and any intervenors, shall file Direct 
Testimony by September 30, 2027. 

Pleadings shall be submitted to Andrew S. Johnston, Executive Secretary, Maryland 
Public Service Commission, William Donald Schaefer Tower, 6 St. Paul Street, 16th 

1 This schedule assumes that the Company will file supplemental direct testimony no later than August 31, 
2026 that addresses the topics listed in PPRP’s Recommendation on Completeness filed in the docket for 
Case 9870 on May 3, 2026 and the Applicant’s Response to PPRP’s Recommendation on Completeness 
filed in the docket for Case 9870 on June 3, 2026. 

3 

Floor, Baltimore, Maryland 21202.1F2 The parties are directed to serve all testimony 
electronically on all parties no later than 5:00 p.m. on the date of the filing; 
(2) 
that the parties shall abide by the discovery procedures set forth in this 
Order; 
(3) 
that, after consultation with the other parties, Potomac Edison is directed 
to contact the Executive Secretary to establish the date and time that a Public Comment 
Hearing will be held in each of the counties affected by the proposed transmission line in 
this matter; 
(4) 
that a Settlement Status/Status Update shall be filed by November 2, 2027; 
and 
(5) 
that a Settlement Evidentiary Hearing (if uncontested) will be held on 
November 16, 2027;2F3 commencement time and location to be determined; 
(6) 
that if the parties do not reach a settlement and contested issues remain, 
then all parties shall file Rebuttal Testimony by a date to be determined; 
(7) 
that if the parties do not reach a settlement and contested issues remain, 
then all parties shall file Surrebuttal Testimony by a date to be determined; 
(8) 
that if the parties do not reach a settlement and contested issues remain, 
then Evidentiary Hearings shall begin on a date to be determined; 3F4 
(9) 
that Initial Briefs shall be filed by a date to be determined; 
(10) 
that Reply Briefs shall be filed by a date to be determined; and 

2 All parties shall use the Commission’s e-file system available on its website, www.psc.maryland.gov, to 
file its pleadings. 
3 If a settlement is reached, then the remainder of this procedural schedule will be adjusted at that time.

The Commission reserves the right to revise the hearing schedule, as needed.
